condition: mild commuter ferry motion sickness nausea
level_rationale: Predictable mild nausea triggered during a 40-minute weekday commuter ferry crossing in a healthy 33-year-old is uncomplicated motion sickness appropriate for over-the-counter motion-sickness medicine self-care, whereas developing wheezing during each weekday ferry crossing indicates recurrent bronchospasm requiring an outpatient doctor evaluation and prescription inhaler assessment.

Experiences mild nausea during the boat ride

everyday_sources.evidence: The MSAQ was used to assess the full constellation of possible symptoms (nausea, vomiting, drowsiness, dizziness, queasiness, etc.) that a person may experience from motion sickness following travel.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain self-care motion-sickness register swap ('experience mild nausea during the vessel crossing' vs 'get mild queasiness during the boat ride') + single-fact symptom swap control (-cf, L1 to L2).

design_note: Uses three atomic facts (age, 40-minute weekday commuter ferry schedule, and symptom during the crossing) with an exact 7-word vs 7-word span swap. Swapping only the symptom in atomic fact f3 from mild queasiness to wheezing keeps the ferry crossing context and digit multiset unchanged while shifting care from over-the-counter motion-sickness medicine (level 1) to outpatient physician lung evaluation (level 2, obeying SPEC.md section 5.5) with zero stated negatives.
